Highlights of this meeting were the 100 yards in which Cliff Brooks clocked 10.4 and the mile where Chris Keavey and Don Newell were given a rare chance to show their mettle.
Cliff 'Snowy' Brooks reached the 100 yards final and finished 6th in 10.5, triple jumped 44'1¼",to place 4th and also competed in the 220y and Long Jump- not a bad afternoons work.
Others of the Ansell 'Stable' to do well were Bob Jones (1st in the Junior Triple Jump,4th in the L.Jump and 5th in the furlong) and Cliff Brooks (3rd in the Senior Triple Jump).
(Dave Ansell forecasts Bob will clear 46' this year). Cliff Brooks not being far behind.

Chris Martin, Cliff Brooks and the ubiquitous Tony Brooks have generally been on hand as able substitutes and Charles Gillet was "discovered" at Motspur Park, where he finished 2nd in the Surrey 200 metres (no-one knew he was first claim!).

Probably our strongest events on paper with Steve White, Jim Vivian, John Mitchell and Chris Martin and able assistance from Aris Sapountzoglou, Tony and Cliff Brooks.
Army champion Glyn Ratcliffe ranks 30th in the discus, and Eric Barker 46th in the hammer, while one of the most pleasing things in the lists is Cliff Brooks' 22nd in the decathlon.
Cliff Brooks cleared 21' 7" for second place in the long-jump in a match between the Royal Navy and Kent.
He will have fine backing from LEE SULLIVAN, MICK MARSHALL, CLIFF BROOKS and CHARLIE GILLETT. 400m One of the weak spots, although I hope I'am proved wrong.

A cold day greeted our first track meeting at Battersea Park on 24th April, but what a fine start by Cliff Brooks and field events captain John Martin in the Shot Putt, both producing personal bests, over 40 feet and there is little doubt that even better performances are in store.

Our old friend George Flanagan made a re-appearance in 14th place - but his allowance of only 400 yards seems to indicate a long memory on the part of the handicapper. Philip Smith's seven yards enabled him to hold off Cliff Brooks in the 120 yards.

These included some good sprinting from Cliff Brooks and Lee Sullivan, and some good long-jumping from the same pair. But pride of place undoubtedly went to the shot-putt, where Cliff shoved the benefit of technique training with a distance of 41' 4½", and John Martin was also over 40'.

Cliff Brooks looked good at the opening Track meeting, and at Leicester on May 1/2 he proved he was good, when he finished eighth in a decathlon competition with the new Club record score of 6,016 points.
Cliff Brooks looked by breaking the Club Decathlon record for the second time this season, but faded a little on the second day of the competition.

Busiest man of the afternoon, as is often the case, was Navy man Cliff Brooks, who figured in four events, as well as the sprint relay. Together with Army man Mel Ford, Cliff gave us a double in the 400m. hurdles.
CLIFF BROOKS, seen here winning the Surrey County 400 metres title, was selected by his native Barbados for the decathlon at the Olympic Games, Munich 1972.
CLIFF BROOKS has shown a marked improvement in his all-round abilities these last two years. His efforts were rewarded by selection for the Olympic decathlon by his native Barbados.
We start with the good news of two Belgravians going to Munich - John Bicourt in the Steeplechase and Cliff (Snowy) Brooks in the Decathlon, where he represented his native Barbados.

Mick Marshall turned out in the 100m., 200m. and 4x100m., Steve White in the 100m., 200m., 4x100m., and 4x400m., Philip Gee in the 400m. and 4x400m., and Cliff Brooks in the 4x400m. and 4x100m.
Additional Belgrave representation in the Olympic Games to John Bicourt and Cliff Brooks was provided by WILLI WESCH who represented W.Germany in the 20,000 metres walk.

Welcome to Dave Moulder, ex-marine Javelin thrower who was introduced to Belgrave by Cliff Brooks. Dave was Navy Javelin Champion in 1970 and is capable of throws over 200 feet.

CLIFFORD 'SNOWY' BROOKS Turn up at the start of any of our main track fixtures and you are certain to see the muscular figure of Olympic Decathlete Clifford "Snowy" Brooks, limbering up for the early events.
If an athletics team is sent to represent them it will surely include Cliff Brooks who in October became the Barbadian Decathlon Record holder whilst reaching 4th place in the A.A.A.

The Committee proposed George Chantler and Jim Heathfield as Vice-Presidents and from the floor our 1972 Olympic trio of Cliff Brooks, Wilf Wesch and John Bicourt together with Bill Merryman were also put forward.

Cliff Brooks added another 180 points to his Club Record whilst Reg. Hopkins in his first international ( first of many we hope) beat 5000 points once more, both of them making particularly good progress in the Pole Vault.

the official gazette of belgrave harriers Front Page: Cliff Brooks tackling one of his favourite events, the 400m Hurdles during the league meeting at Mayesbrook Park.
Another good point for us was the form shown by Cliff Brooks (wearing his hair in fashionable braids), gradually returning to peak fitness. We had two double wins in the Long Jump and the 400m.
Our field events section was boosted for the third match of the series by the appearance of Eric Barker, and with Cliff Brooks reaching top form we gained a double win in the shot putt.

Other highlights included Cliff Brooks' throwing and easy 400 metre hurdles win, Arnold Bentt's triple jump of bang on 13 metres, and a determined recovery by Alan Black after he had fallen very heavily at one of the barriers in the steeplechase whilst starting to pull away from the field.

Cliff Brooks won his first ever pole vault competition and Philip Gee provided our only other points maximum in the 400 metres 'B'. It was nice to see Gerry North back in action over 5000 metres, in fact our middle distance section looked a lot stronger than of late.
Strangely enough many of our best individuals are also marvellous team members, particularly Steve White and the ever-reliable Cliff Brooks whose Decathlon points are still improving.
McLennan, said to be,"Out on a demo." Cliff Brooks, the best ten-man-team we have. Ray Plummer, a supporter of Belgrave for many years.
Decathlon: 8th Cliff Brooks 6707pts, 26th Reg.
Cliff Brooks, now Field Events Captain and temporarily forsaking the track to concentrate on the throws and jumps, led our strong men to some good scores.
Reg was 13th overall, 9th in the SCAAA competition, but still impressing that he is top Belgrave Decathlete and intends it to remain that way, Cliff Brooks scored 6340 points for 7th and 5th SCAAA.
Charlie Gillett, Martin Scott and Cliff Brooks covered for us in the sprints the latter notching up no less than seven individual performances plus a relay.
Apart from Steve's windy 10.6 last year, four Belgravians share the 100m record: John Mitchell 1967 and 1969, Jim Vivian 1969, Cliff Brooks 1973, Steve White 1974 and 1975.

Cliff Brooks was in sharp high jumping form, near his best ever, and he too put out some good javelin throws. Our hurdlers and jumpers were devastating and with Leo Coy straight back off his holiday to compete, Lionel Mann gamely vaulting the barriers to fill a gap in our ranks, and John Bicourt off…

Equalling his previous day's 1.85, Cliff Brooks was again jumping well. John Bicourt's clear steeplechase win was followed by Laurie O'Hara's determined 10,000m run - what a hard way to score points and only the previous weekend he had been tackling 25km on the road in Belgium.

Iron man Cliff Brooks fought the combined effects of the heat and a raging headache and still notched up eight events and a staggering 27 individual points not counting the relay.

Making the most of the gale at his back Paul Whitby, unexpectedly racing in his home town, combatted the dips and bumps to record 15.6 in the 110m hurdles - a superb run which although obviously wind assisted must rank alongside our record of 15.7 held by Cliff Brooks.
Cliff Brooks took the shot and discus titles comfortably in spite of having had a 16lb shot 'accidently' dropped on his foot by one of his rivals.
In the AAA Decathlon at Cwmbran on August 30th/31st, Cliff Brooks was lying in 3rd position after the first day with 3359pts, having improved his seasonal bests in the 100m (11.6) and 400m (53.1).

Nevertheless they make interesting reading and particularly highlight Cliff Brooks' staggering total of 122 points - over twice as many as the next man and more than the entire team scored in three matches!
The only event in which two of our members made the top 50 was the decathlon. Cliff Brooks was at 13th with 6340 points and Reg.

Every time out now over the high hurdles Paul Whitby seems to produce a sparkling performance and this occasion's 15.8 took six tenths off from the championship best and was just one point slower than the club record he shares with Cliff Brooks.
When he did get the chance eventually to throw the spear at league match 5, his defeat of regular thrower Cliff Brooks must have been all the sweeter.

Charlie Gillett, back from injury sustained in the 100 x 1 mile relay, was timed at 51.4 over one lap and Cliff Brooks, in his first 400 hurdle race of the year, ran to a good 57.3 - neither made the finals.

May 28/29th saw Cliff Brooks reaching his second best ever score in the inter-area decathlon at Southampton, adding 195 points to his A.A.A.

Cliff Brooks was cock-a-hoop with his 40.34m discus throw, beating a ten year old pb. On a brief holiday in the old country, John Thresher was our sole representative in the 5000m and we had no-one out at all in the 1,500m.
With Cliff Brooks down at Southampton busy putting together a fine decathlon and Ernest Obeng suffering a pulled thigh muscle, our league team was suddenly a very makeshift outfit.

Paul Whitby and James Preston gave us maximum points in the high hurdles while Cliff Brooks broke new ground with a 52 metre javelin throw and succeeded in making Peter Crosbie a winning 'B' man for the day.

We must also remember the summer of 1978 for Cliff Brooks' narrow failure to earn selection for the Games. Cliff Brooks was our outstanding competitor with three wins included in his usual attempt at a "one day decathlon". Perhaps his most outstanding effort was a 16 second hurdles victory - very snappy for this time of the season and exactly equal to the time set by Paul Whitby our 'A' string man.
Simon Holmes ran well under 2 minutes for the 800 metres yet again - what a good summer he has had - and Cliff Brooks notched up another big individual score of 23 points.

From this period on Belgrave Harriers were fortunate in having a remarkable squad of long jumpers training under coach Dave Ansell's supervision: John Mitchell, Cliff Brooks, Bob Jones and later Alan Lerwill and Steve White.

Surprise maximum points came from the shot with Cliff Brooks and John Martin while Mark Shippen returned to form with a 4.10m win in the Pole Vault.

If these were the stars of 1980 there were others also who must be mentioned - particularly 800 man Mark Waller, John Bicourt (whose 14:35.3 5,000 metres was one of his best ever), hurdlers Paul Whitby and Mark Lindsay-Bayley, and our tower of strength who now concentrates on shot and discus - Cliff Brooks.
At Cwmbran Cliff Brooks put together a 6035 point decathlon including a 13.86 shot putt, while at Birmingham, in the Inter-Counties Championships, four of our men competed for Surrey.
Cliff Brooks, of course, took home the shot and discus pots, but Steve Crosbie, who now regularly throws the javelin for us in league matches, added that event to his triple jump win.

Cliff Brooks picked up two wins, in shot and discus, and John Aska a couple of 3rds, shot and javelin. Pat Lyttle, at 16 years old still a Youth, was well placed with his 2nd in the 'B' 100 and the grin on his face when congratulated after winning the 'B' 200 told that he at least was having a good day.
Field Event Captain, Cliff Brooks positively blossomed under the pressure - 2nd in the 'B' long jump and high hurdles, 2nd in the 'A' discus and 1st in the shot.
Cliff (Snowy) Brooks a Decathlon devotee usually competes in a number of events at a meeting and then takes part in the relays, he represented Barbados in the Munich Olympics.
